newsitem.title: USA: Farm Credit Banks see Orange Cty suit as meritless.
newsitem.headline: Farm Credit Banks see Orange Cty suit as meritless.

text.p: The Federal Farm Credit System said on Tuesday that it considered Orange County, Calif.,'s bankruptcy-related lawsuit against eight system banks to be without merit.

The county sued eight Farm Credit System Banks in December in U.S. Bankruptcy Court, alleging that offering documents for certain Farm Credit System debt issues purchased by the county contained material misrepresentations and omissions that contributed to the county's market losses and bankruptcy.

In a statement issued on Tuesday, the Federal Farm Credit Banks Funding Corp, which serves as the fiscal agent of the System Banks, said it believed the disclosures and types of transactions referred to in Orange County's lawsuit were in compliance with securities laws.

"The Farm Credit System Banks are considering various options as to how best to respond to this obvious and inappropriate effort by Orange County to seek to recoup the county's market losses," a spokesperson for the Federal Farm Credit Banks Funding Corp said.
The spokesperson said the System Banks expected to prevail in the lawsuit, but that it was too soon to determine the potential financial impact, if any, of the legal action.

The Banks have until March 7 to respond to the county's lawsuit, which did not specify damages. Orange County has filed similar suits against several other government-sponsored enterprises that issued securities purchased by the county.
The county filed for bankruptcy protection on Dec. 6, 1994, after sustaining losses of more than $1.6 billion on risky investments.
The county emerged from bankruptcy in last June.
